clue.text: Answer with wit about my and others' not being tailed

parts.note: A is the standard abbreviation for answer

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for wit wraps around the possessive

parts.note: nous is common sense or native wit
the possessive belonging to me and others together

explanation.surface: A quip about how we, unlike others, are not being followed by a tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My and others'' is a roundabout way of saying the first-person plural possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Anourous is the zoological term for animals lacking a tail, such as frogs once grown.

clue.text: Maybe Sillitoe's written contrarily about very critical ward, which keeps church incensed?

indicators.note: about means around, so the backwards name surrounds the other pieces
contrarily means the opposite way, so the writer's name is written backwards

parts.note: Alan Sillitoe wrote Saturday Night and Sunday Morning
V is the abbreviation for very
the intensive care unit is where critical patients go

explanation.surface: A novelist, writing perversely about a hospital ward, enrages the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incensed' looks like angry but means supplied with incense. NALA goes around V + ICU.
explanation.definitionFit: A navicula is the boat-shaped vessel holding incense for the thurible, supplying the church with incense.

clue.text: Large vehicle boxed in by French one which took off, still victorious?

indicators.note: boxed in means hemmed in on both sides, so the vehicle sits between the French words

parts.note: un is French for one
a van is a large road vehicle
qui is French for which, carried over from French
to shed is to take off, as clothes

explanation.surface: A van hemmed in by a French plane that took off, yet still the winner?
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' governs both the word for one and the word for which, and the vehicle sits between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Unvanquished means never defeated, so someone who has kept on winning to date.

clue.text: Humorously defeats judge in Open University trials

parts.note: OU is the Open University

indicators.note: in places the judge inside the other letters

parts.note: tests are trials
J is the abbreviation for judge

explanation.surface: A judge wittily beats rivals in Open University examinations.
explanation.walkthrough: The Open University is Britain's distance-learning university.
explanation.definitionFit: To outjest someone is to beat them in banter, getting the better of them through jokes.

clue.text: Sound of packing snow, say, with school crossing cold ski slope

indicators.note: crossing as in straddling, so the school word spans the other pieces

parts.note: SCH is the abbreviation for school
C is the abbreviation for cold
a ski run is a slope

explanation.surface: The crunch of compacted snow as a school party crosses a chilly piste.
explanation.walkthrough: SCH straddles C + RUN: S(CRUN)CH.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrunch is the crunching noise made by treading on compressed snow or gravel, an example of such a sound.

clue.text: Kit initially seen on eg Man Utd for a month

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: first letter of kit
the Isle of Man is an example of an isle
U is short for United

explanation.surface: A football strip seen on a Manchester United player for a month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man Utd' looks like the football club; Man is the island and Utd gives U.
explanation.definitionFit: Kisleu is an older spelling of Kislev, the third month of the Jewish civil year.

clue.text: Head dismissed by big boss

indicators.note: the head of the word is its front, and dismissing it drops the first letter

parts.note: jumbo means very big

explanation.surface: A senior executive sacked by the big boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' looks like the chief but is a raised knob. JUMBO loses its J.
explanation.definitionFit: An umbo is the raised central knob on a shield, also called its boss.

clue.text: Bit of broken vessel or tank, so battered

indicators.note: something battered is knocked about, so these letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A fragment of a wrecked ship or tank that has been badly battered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: An ostrakon is a potsherd, a piece of broken pottery used in ancient Greece for voting on ostracism.

clue.text: Mate with no new problems rebutted contrasting rhetoric

indicators.note: with no new tells us to drop the letter standing for new from the word for mate

parts.note: china plate is rhyming slang for mate, shortened to china
N is the abbreviation for new

indicators.note: rebutted suggests being pushed back, so the word for problems runs backwards

parts.note: sums are arithmetic problems

explanation.surface: A mate, freed of new difficulties, retorts with a piece of contrasting speech.
explanation.walkthrough: China (from the rhyming slang china plate = mate) loses its N to give CHIA, then SUMS reversed gives SMUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A chiasmus is a figure of speech in which two parallel phrases have their terms inverted, setting ideas against each other.

clue.text: Stopping to dwell briefly, see city in Ukraine

indicators.note: stopping as in filling a gap, so the shortened verb plugs around the other piece
briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the verb for dwell goes

parts.note: to dwell is to live somewhere
V is short for vide, Latin for see

explanation.surface: Pausing to linger a while and take in a Ukrainian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' as V comes from the Latin vide, used in reference books.
explanation.definitionFit: Lviv is the large historic city in western Ukraine, formerly known as Lemberg or Lvov.

clue.text: Usual juror Joe surprisingly hasn't succeeded in meeting immediate needs

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters turn up in an unexpected order
hasn't tells us the letter for succeeded is missing from the words

parts.note: the letters taken as written
S is the abbreviation for succeeded

explanation.surface: An ordinary juror called Joe has, surprisingly, failed to get by.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase au jour le jour means from day to day, living hand to mouth on present needs only.

clue.text: Pound of muscle protein, with pound brought down under Callaghan, familiarly

indicators.note: brought down means moved lower, so that letter leaves its place and drops further down the word

parts.note: James Callaghan, British prime minister, known as Jim
myoglobin is the oxygen-carrying protein in muscle
the second pound in the clue: L is its abbreviation, from libra

explanation.surface: A pound of muscle protein as sterling was devalued under Prime Minister Callaghan.
explanation.walkthrough: In MYOGLOBIN the L moves down two places to give MYOGOBLIN, which goes under JIM in this down entry. Jimmy o'goblin is rhyming slang for sovereign.
explanation.definitionFit: Jimmy o'goblin is rhyming slang for a sovereign, the gold coin worth one pound sterling.

clue.text: Half-square threaded back through woman's underwear and loose outerwear

indicators.note: threaded through means woven in alternately among the letters of the underwear
back tells us the kept part runs the other way
half means only the first part of the word for square is kept

parts.note: taken as written; its first half is SQU
a bra is an item of underwear
surface padding: the woman whose underwear it is adds no letters

explanation.surface: A half-square of fabric is sewn back into lingerie and some loose garments.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed half-square is not dropped in as one chunk: its letters alternate with those of the underwear, one after each, like a thread weaving in and out.
explanation.definitionFit: Burqas are loose garments that cover a woman's whole body, worn over other clothes in some Muslim traditions.

clue.text: Crook's lousy chat declining each year

indicators.note: declining means refusing, so each word refuses its letter for year

parts.note: crummy means poor or lousy
to yack is to chatter
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A criminal's poor small talk getting worse with every passing year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crook' looks like a criminal but is a shepherd's staff. Each of CRUMMY and YACK loses its Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A crummack is a Scots word for a shepherd's crook or a stick with a hooked head.

clue.text: Spicy paste ingredient of Bihari's sauces

indicators.note: an ingredient is something inside a mixture, so the answer sits inside the following words

parts.note: inside biHARI'S SAuces

explanation.surface: A hot paste that goes into the sauces of someone from Bihar.
explanation.definitionFit: Harissa is a hot North African chilli paste used to season stews and couscous.

clue.text: Muscat raised as an introduction: how nice!

indicators.note: raised in a down entry means written upwards, so the order runs backwards

parts.note: to open is to serve as an introduction
ah is a sigh of pleasure

explanation.surface: A toast with muscat wine raised as an opening, followed by a contented sigh.
explanation.walkthrough: TO OPEN + AH, written upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanepoot is the South African name for the muscat of Alexandria grape and its sweet wine.

clue.text: Vary one's working in French Department

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are being worked over into a new shape

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone changing their job in a French government ministry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Department' looks like a ministry but is one of the administrative regions of France.
explanation.definitionFit: Aveyron is a département in southern France, in the Occitanie region, named after its river.

clue.text: White hellebore or green lily with a central inversion

indicators.note: a central inversion turns round the two middle letters of the joined words

parts.note: vert is heraldic green
the arum lily

explanation.surface: Choosing between a pale hellebore and a green lily with an odd twist in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: VERT + ARUM gives VERTARUM, and swapping its central TA gives the answer. 'Or' looks like an alternative but merely links.
explanation.definitionFit: Veratrum is the genus of poisonous plants including white hellebore, Veratrum album.

clue.text: Aggressive call on jerk roughly fencing island's nut tree

indicators.note: fencing means enclosing, so the jerk and roughly words surround the island

parts.note: oi is a rude shout to get attention
a tic is an involuntary jerk
I is the abbreviation for island
ca is circa, roughly

explanation.surface: Someone yells at a lout who roughly encloses an island's walnut tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerk roughly' together forms the fence, with the island between its two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: The oiticica is a Brazilian tree whose nuts yield a drying oil used in paints and varnishes.

clue.text: Shakespearean bighead such as Hal or Hamlet cut down bovine creature

indicators.note: cut down means trimmed, so the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: Prince Hal and Prince Hamlet
an ox is a bovine animal

explanation.surface: Two Shakespeare princes, both conceited, bring down a bull.
explanation.definitionFit: Princox is Capulet's word for an insolent, conceited youth in Romeo and Juliet, a coxcomb.

clue.text: Swift's relative rejection of governor's lead in Indian rule, weak

indicators.note: rejection throws the whole assembly back, so it reads the other way

parts.note: the Raj was British rule in India

indicators.note: in places that single letter inside the following words

parts.note: thin as in feeble or weak

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its front, so only its first letter is used

parts.note: first letter of governor

explanation.surface: A satirical writer's relation turns down a colonial governor's leadership of a feeble Indian administration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swift's' looks like Jonathan Swift but is the bird. G goes into RAJ THIN to give RAJTHGIN, which reversed is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightjars and swifts are both insect-eating birds once grouped in a closely related order.

clue.text: Old cab driver's clash with rival

parts.note: to jar is to clash, as colours or sounds
to vie is to compete, to rival

explanation.surface: A former taxi driver's run-in with a competitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A jarvie was a Scots term for a hackney coachman, the driver of a cab for hire.

clue.text: Perhaps size of crowd paying to see rugby featuring rucks

parts.note: RU is short for rugby union
the gate is the number of paying spectators at a match

explanation.surface: How many fans paid to watch a rugby match full of rucks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rucks' looks like rugby scrums but means creases. The pieces sit in reverse clue order: the gate is what pays to see RU.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugate is a botanical and zoological adjective meaning wrinkled or ridged, so covered in creases.

clue.text: Due to drink wine over time in boozer's vat full of preservative?

indicators.note: to drink is to take something inside, so the first word swallows the second

parts.note: a boozer is British slang for a pub

indicators.note: in places all of the preceding inside the boozer

parts.note: owing means due, as of a debt

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the wine word runs backwards

parts.note: red is red wine
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Something owed for drinking wine during closing time at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The wine goes inside the word for due, time is added, and everything sits inside the pub after its first letter. A boozer is British slang for a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A powdering tub was a tub in which meat was salted down to preserve it, with salt as the preservative.

clue.text: Scots point the finger at husks of woolly thistle

indicators.note: husks are the outer casings, so only the outside letters of each word are taken

parts.note: first and last letters of woolly
first and last letters of thistle

explanation.surface: Scottish folk blame the fluffy outer casings of a thistle, Scotland's emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: Wyte is a Scots verb meaning to blame, accuse or reproach someone for a fault.

clue.text: Dormouse stretched out in gloomier setting?

indicators.note: stretched out in a setting means the letters wanted are set inside the next word but spaced apart rather than packed together

parts.note: second letter
third letter
sixth letter
eighth letter

explanation.surface: A small rodent lies sprawled asleep somewhere darker.
explanation.walkthrough: A hidden word with a twist: the letters run in order through the word but not side by side, so the dormouse is itself stretched out across it.
explanation.definitionFit: The loir is the edible or fat dormouse of Europe, once fattened as a Roman delicacy.

clue.text: An inferior wine's too much to start with in miniature flute

parts.note: OTT is over the top
the indefinite article
vino is cheap wine

explanation.surface: Cheap wine being excessive to begin with in a tiny flute glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To start with' puts OTT at the front of A VINO. 'Flute' looks like a champagne glass but is the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The ottavino is the Italian name for the piccolo, the small flute pitched an octave higher.

clue.text: Eleven intend to include outsiders thereof, according to cryptic crossword principles

parts.note: XI is eleven in Roman numerals, and a cricket team

indicators.note: include puts those letters inside the word for intend

parts.note: to mean is to intend

indicators.note: outsiders are the letters on the outside, the first and last of the word referred to

parts.note: first and last letters of the word eleven

explanation.surface: A team of eleven plans to bring in outsiders, as cryptic setters' rules allow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thereof' points back to Eleven, so its first and last letters are the ones taken in.
explanation.definitionFit: Ximenean describes clueing that follows the strict fairness rules set out by Ximenes, the Observer setter D S Macnutt.
